page_title: A Simple Web App in Rust, Part 1

summary.title: A Simple Web App in Rust, Part 1
summary.one_liner: Follow a Rust beginner building a tiny Nickel-based "hello world" web server, covering Cargo project setup, the router! macro, and the function return-type and semicolon errors encountered along the way.
takeaways: How to install Rust via Homebrew and check that rustc and cargo work
How to create a Cargo binary project and add a git dependency on nickel.rs
How a minimal Nickel server is set up with the router! macro and listens on 127.0.0.1:6767
Why a trailing semicolon in a Rust function body changes its return value and causes a type mismatch with the declared return type
The author's plan: build separate small programs first, then combine them and deploy to a VPS
summary.summary: The author, an experienced programmer new to Rust, writes a stream-of-consciousness log of building a tiny web app that will record daily medication visits. The post installs Rust with Homebrew, runs a hello world, and sets up a Cargo project with a nickel.rs git dependency. It then walks through running the Nickel example and refactoring the response into a say_hello function, where a semicolon and a missing return type cause compiler errors that get fixed. The page is an early part of a series and ends by previewing writing the current date to a file.
